title: Mechanical separation with aqueous washing
summary: The butt is broken up and washed in water, so that the cellulose acetate filter fraction is separated from the paper, tobacco and ash, and the surface residues are carried away in the wash water.
mechanism: Two variants sit in this family. In staged washing, butts are washed in water and then optionally in ethanol, and the filter material is recovered without being dissolved. In the grinding route, butts are milled so that the filter fraction separates from the paper and tobacco matrix, sieved out, washed in water, dried and milled again into fibrous particles. In both variants the question is the same: whether washing removes contaminants from the fibre or only redistributes them between fibre, water and sludge.
feedstock: Collected whole spent cigarette butts, including filter, paper and residual tobacco. The mass basis of a collected lot is not stated by any located source, and it is not established whether butts must be dry before processing.
preparation: Drying where the lot is wet, then either direct washing or grinding and sieving to separate the filter fraction from the paper, tobacco and ash fraction.

steps.label: Collection and drying
steps.description: Spent cigarette butts are collected from ash trays, bins or street litter and dried where the lot is wet. No located source states a moisture content or a drying protocol for collected butts.

steps.label: Separation of the filter fraction
steps.description: In the grinding variant, butts are milled so that the plastic filter separates from the tobacco and paper matrix, and sieves recover the filter fraction while the paper, tobacco and ash fraction is rejected as a separate stream. No located source states a particle size, a sieve aperture, or how much of the fines fraction is lost with the rejected stream.

steps.label: Aqueous wash
steps.description: The filter fraction is agitated in water so that surface dust, loose tobacco and dissolved residues are carried into the wash water. Some described designs use more than one wash tank in sequence and recycle the wash water. No located source states a wash temperature, a contact time, a water-to-feed ratio, or whether the recycled water receives any treatment or purge.

steps.label: Optional ethanol wash
steps.description: In the staged variant, a second wash in ethanol is used for residues that water does not dissolve. No located source states an ethanol concentration, a ratio or a recovery method, and this step is described only in the literature and company material, not in a located operating record.

steps.label: Drying and size reduction
steps.description: The washed material is dried and may be milled into a fibrous or particulate form. The batch-02 source documents give illustrative temperature ranges for drying and state that these are inventor choices rather than measured reference values; no located source states a drying protocol.

inputs.label: Collected spent cigarette butts
inputs.description: Whole collected butts, including the filter, the paper wrapper, residual tobacco and ash.

inputs.label: Process water
inputs.description: Wash water, some described designs recovering it through a closed loop with a limited capacity per cycle.

inputs.label: Ethanol, optional
inputs.description: Used in the staged variant only, to dissolve residues that water does not.

streams.label: Rejected paper, tobacco and ash fraction
Fines carried away with the rejected stream

products.label: Washed cellulose acetate fibre
products.description: Dried, optionally milled filter material recovered after washing. Its residual contaminant content and mechanical properties are not established by any located source.
products.intendedUse: Not established. No product standard accepts washed filter material for any stated use.

sinks.material: Cellulose acetate recovered from cigarette filters, in a material split reported by a company rather than a product specification.
sinks.intendedUse: A composite filler and, in one described route, thermo-compressed sheets for outdoor furniture. Use-compliance is not demonstrated by any located source.
sinks.acceptanceBasis: Not established. No product gate, leaching test or regulatory acceptance has been located for this material.
sinks.issuer: Not established. No company, standard body or authority has been located as the issuer of an accepted product.
sinks.finalRoute: Not established. The wash water, the rejected solids and the sludge have no demonstrated final disposal route in any located source.

organizations.name: MéGo!
organizations.role: Company whose located patent describes a collection network and a grinding, washing, water-recycling, drying and milling route, and whose environmental assessment is described as not publicly available.

organizations.name: Re-Cig
organizations.role: Company whose documents are described as covering a recycled-content declaration model, an end-of-waste annex with a product specification, and organisational rather than product-level certification.

claims.title: A published study describes staged water and ethanol washing of cigarette filters
claims.proposition: A published study describes extracting spent cigarette filters in hot water, rinsing them with cold water and then washing them with ethanol, and reports recovering cellulose acetate from that sequence.

claims.title: A patent describes grinding, washing, water recycling, drying and milling of cigarette butts
claims.proposition: A granted patent describes a route in which cigarette butts are ground, sieved so that the filter fraction is separated, washed with water, dried and milled again, with the wash water recovered through a closed loop.

claims.title: Published material-split figures for this family carry no mass basis and conflict with each other
claims.proposition: Figures published for this family give a material split into filter material, wash residues and rejected solids, and a figure for butt mass per kilogram, but none of them states whether the mass was measured wet or dry, and two published figures for butt mass per kilogram disagree with each other.

claims.title: No located source reports contaminant removal data for this family
claims.proposition: No located source reports how much of each named contaminant leaves the filter material in each wash stage, or what remains in the washed fibre, for this family.

claims.title: No located source states where metals go in this family
claims.proposition: No located source states the fate of heavy metals in this family, and no located source demonstrates a metals-removal outcome or a lawful route for metal-bearing residue.

claims.title: No jurisdiction-specific regulatory status has been located for this family
claims.proposition: No located source names a jurisdiction, a material status, an acceptance pathway or an authority for this family, so the regulatory position of the recovered material remains unlocated.

claims.title: The located descriptions of this family do not establish contaminant removal
claims.proposition: Because the located description of this family sets out the separation and washing steps but reports no contaminant removal figures for them, the family cannot be compared with any other family on contaminant fate.
claims.reasoning: Both located sources describe the process sequence. Neither states a removal figure for any named contaminant, so the sequence can be reported but its effect cannot be compared. The absence of a removal figure is recorded here as an absence, not as a small removal.

gaps.title: Does washing remove contaminants from the fibre or only redistribute them
gaps.question: When this family washes cigarette butts, do the contaminants leave with the wash water and the rejected solids, or do they stay bound in the cellulose acetate that becomes the product?
gaps.whyItMatters: The whole value of the route depends on the answer. If the contaminants redistribute rather than leave, then the product carries the same contaminant burden in a different place, and the wash water becomes a concentrated stream that needs a route of its own.
gaps.falsifierOrDecisionCondition: A measurement of the same named analytes in the input lot, in each wash liquor and in the washed fibre, on one dry-mass basis, would either close this question or show that the contaminants stay with the fibre.

gaps.title: A closed wash-water loop without a stated purge concentrates contaminants
gaps.question: How should the recycled wash water in this family be treated before it is used again?
gaps.whyItMatters: A loop that reuses wash water without a stated purge or treatment step is a concentrating loop: what leaves the fibre accumulates in the water that is used to wash the next lot.
assumptions: The recycled water is used on more than one batch, as the located description implies.
No treatment step other than settling is applied between uses, because no located source describes one.
gaps.falsifierOrDecisionCondition: If a located source described the treatment applied to the recycled water, or a measured purge, then the concentrating effect would be bounded rather than open, and this note would no longer hold.

assessments.title: Evidence strength for mechanical and physical washing
assessments.label: Limited
assessments.rationale: The located support is a granted patent and a peer-reviewed extraction study, both first-party or narrowly scoped, with no independent verification of any performance claim and no published removal data. That places the family in the limited band rather than the minimal band, because direct descriptions of the process do exist.

assessments.title: Process ease for mechanical and physical washing
assessments.label: Moderate
assessments.rationale: The described sequence uses common equipment and a short set of steps, but it depends on sieving that has to separate a fine filter fraction from a fine paper and ash fraction, and on wash-water handling. Neither difficulty is severe enough to make the route very difficult.

assessments.title: Resource burden for mechanical and physical washing
assessments.unknownReason: No located source reports water or energy consumption on a stated functional unit, and no comparable denominator exists across the families, so this criterion stays unknown rather than being estimated from the appearance of the process.

assessments.title: Contaminant fate coverage for mechanical and physical washing
assessments.label: Minimal
assessments.rationale: The decision-relevant analytes and the major output streams have not been measured. A completed review located descriptions of the streams but no measurement of their contaminant content, which is what the lowest band describes.

assessments.title: Sink completeness for mechanical and physical washing
assessments.label: Proposed
assessments.rationale: The material and an intended route are named, but no acceptance basis and no issuer have been located for the washed material, and the wash water and rejected solids have no demonstrated final route.

assessments.title: Product readiness for mechanical and physical washing
assessments.label: Undefined
assessments.rationale: No product identity, quality property, leaching behaviour or product gate has been located for the washed material, so there is nothing to judge readiness against.

assessments.title: Regulatory clarity for mechanical and physical washing
assessments.label: Unlocated
assessments.rationale: No located source names a jurisdiction, a material status, or an authority that would regulate this material as a product rather than as waste. A company-level end-of-waste annex exists for one operator, but it is not a regulatory pathway.

assessments.title: Validation maturity for mechanical and physical washing
assessments.label: Foundational unknowns
assessments.rationale: The partition itself is unresolved: whether washing removes or redistributes the contaminants is a basic question that has to be answered before a bounded test against any product criterion can even be designed.

gapNotes: No published protocol specifies wash temperatures, agitation speeds, the number of stages, water-to-butt ratios or drying temperatures for this family. Those parameters are inventor choices, not measured reference values.

No analyte-resolved mass balance exists for this family. It is not known what share of nicotine, tar components, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons or heavy metals leaves with each wash liquor, or what remains in the washed material.
No energy or water consumption data exists for this family at any scale. The per-unit denominators cannot be estimated without measurements.
The washed material has not been characterised for mechanical properties, thermal stability or residual toxicity, and no product standard accepts it.
No regulatory pathway has been identified for this material. Local waste and environmental rules would have to be checked before any trial.
No cost data exists for this family. Solvent recovery, wastewater treatment and material yield would dominate the operating economics, and all three are unmeasured.
Evidence for this family is limited to company descriptions and patent mentions. No independent verification of any performance claim exists.
This family cannot close a four-field sink with the evidence located so far. All four fields are open.

fourField.dryMassBalance: Unknown - no mass-balance data has been published for this family.
fourField.analyteFate: Unknown - no per-analyte removal data has been published for this family.
fourField.treatmentRoute: Not defined - no final disposition route has been specified for the wash water or the rejected solids.
fourField.productGate: Not set - no product acceptance criteria have been established for the washed material.

title: Dry treatment and composite extrusion
summary: The butt is dried and size-reduced without any washing, then blended into a plastic matrix and extruded into profiles. The contaminants are not removed; they are sealed inside the composite.
mechanism: Drying, milling and blending into a thermoplastic binder, followed by extrusion into profiles such as planks, posts and panels. No washing stage is used, so the filter material and paper stay physically embedded in the plastic and the contaminants travel with them into the product.
feedstock: Spent cigarette butts, dried, combined with a thermoplastic resin such as polyethylene or polypropylene. No located source states the blend ratio between butt material and binder, and no located source states a mass basis for the butt fraction.
preparation: Drying the butts, then milling them to a fibrous or particulate form suitable for blending with the binder.
variants: dry size reduction and extrusion into a thermoplastic composite

steps.label: Drying
steps.description: Butts are dried so that moisture does not disrupt the extrusion step. No located source states a drying protocol or a moisture target.

steps.label: Size reduction
steps.description: The dried butts are milled to a fibrous or particulate form that can be blended with the binder. No located source states a particle size distribution.

steps.label: Blending into a binder matrix
steps.description: The milled material is mixed with a thermoplastic resin, sometimes with additives such as coupling agents or stabilisers. No located source states a blend ratio or a formulation.

steps.label: Extrusion into profiles
steps.description: The blend is melted and formed into profiles, then cooled and cut. The located company description gives an illustrative melting range and states that it is not a measured reference value.

steps.label: End of life
steps.description: No located source names a route for the composite at end of life. Burning a composite that contains butt material would release what was sealed inside it.

inputs.label: Dried spent cigarette butts
inputs.description: Dried butt material for use as a composite filler.

inputs.label: Thermoplastic binder
inputs.description: Virgin or recycled polyethylene or polypropylene used to carry the butt material.

products.label: Extruded composite profiles
products.description: Planks, posts and panels made from butt material bound in a thermoplastic matrix, offered for outdoor furniture and construction.
products.intendedUse: Outdoor furniture and construction products are named by the operator, but no located source demonstrates fitness for a load-bearing application and no product standard accepts this material.

sinks.material: Thermoplastic composite containing dried cigarette butt material, at a blend ratio that no located source states.
sinks.intendedUse: Street furniture and construction profiles, as claimed by the operator.
sinks.acceptanceBasis: Not established. No product standard, building-code provision or leaching limit has been located for this composite.
sinks.issuer: Not established. No company, standard body or authority has been located as the issuer of an accepted product.
sinks.finalRoute: Not established. No route for the composite at end of life has been located, and burning it would release the encapsulated residues.

organizations.name: Keenat
organizations.role: Company whose materials describe the dry treatment and extrusion-composite route and claim outdoor furniture products, without independent performance or lifecycle data.

claims.title: A company describes a dry route that blends butt material into a thermoplastic composite
claims.proposition: Company materials describe a process in which cigarette butts are dried and size-reduced, blended with a thermoplastic binder and extruded into composite profiles, with no washing stage.

claims.title: This family contains the contaminants rather than removing them
claims.proposition: Because this family uses no washing or dissolution stage, the contaminants in the butt material remain inside the composite, and what can leave the product later is a question of leaching and weathering rather than of removal.
claims.reasoning: The located description has no stage at which a contaminant could leave the material, so the contamination stays with the product. Whether it later escapes the product is a separate and unmeasured question, so this proposition is an inference from the absence of a removal stage rather than a measured result.

claims.title: No located source reports leaching or weathering behaviour for this family
claims.proposition: No located source reports whether contaminants leach from the composite under weathering, rain or temperature cycling, and no located source reports the emissions from processing butt material in this way.

claims.title: Heavy metals are not removed by this family
claims.proposition: No located source reports the heavy-metal content of this composite or its leaching potential, and no located source describes a step in this family that would remove heavy metals.

claims.title: No jurisdiction-specific regulatory status has been located for this family
claims.proposition: No located source names a jurisdiction, a material status, an acceptance pathway or an authority for this family, so the regulatory position of the recovered material remains unlocated.

claims.title: This family cannot be compared with other families on contaminant fate
claims.proposition: Because this family contains the contaminants rather than treating them, comparing it with a washing or dissolution family on contaminant fate would compare a containment step with a treatment step, and no located source supports such a comparison.
claims.reasoning: A contaminant-fate comparison assumes that each route moves contaminants in some describable way. Here the located description gives no transfer step at all, so the family has no fate to compare. The comparison is therefore withheld rather than scored.

gaps.title: Do contaminants stay inside the composite for the life of the product
gaps.question: If the contaminants are sealed inside the composite rather than removed, do they stay there for the life of the product, or do they migrate out under rain, heat and ultraviolet exposure?
gaps.whyItMatters: The route's entire environmental argument rests on containment holding for as long as the product is in use. If it does not hold, the product becomes a slow source of the same contaminants it was made from.
gaps.falsifierOrDecisionCondition: A leaching study that measures the named analytes in the composite over time under stated exposure conditions would either show that containment holds or show that it does not.

gaps.title: A dense-fluid extraction route has no reviewed method page in this layer
gaps.question: A dense pressurized-fluid extraction route for cigarette butts is recorded in the project's method record, but it has not been given a reviewed method-family page in this layer. What does it do, and how does it compare with the dry composite route?
gaps.whyItMatters: The reader would otherwise take this page as a complete account of thermal routes, when one thermal route has been described in the project's records and not yet assessed here.
gaps.falsifierOrDecisionCondition: A reviewed method page, with its own claims, gaps and assessments, would close this gap and show where the route sits against the dry composite route.

gaps.title: Containment is not removal
gaps.question: Should the composite route be described as a recycling route at all?
gaps.whyItMatters: If the contaminants travel into the product and the product is then used outdoors, the route changes the form of the waste rather than the amount of it, and calling that recycling without qualification would mislead a reader.
assumptions: The product is used in the open, as the claimed street-furniture applications imply.
No later treatment removes the contaminants once the composite is in service.
gaps.falsifierOrDecisionCondition: If a located source demonstrated that the contaminants are removed or immobilised to a defined standard before or during use, the route could be described as treatment; until then the description stays as containment.

assessments.label: Limited
assessments.rationale: The located support is company material and general composite literature, with no independent verification of product performance, safety or environmental benefit, and no analyte or leaching data.

assessments.label: Moderate
assessments.rationale: Drying, milling, blending and extrusion are standard industrial operations with widely available equipment, and no specialised control beyond extrusion itself is described, which keeps the route clear of the difficult band without making it simple.

assessments.title: Resource burden for dry treatment and composite extrusion
assessments.unknownReason: No located source reports energy consumption for drying, milling or extrusion on a stated functional unit, and no comparable denominator exists across the families, so this criterion stays unknown.

assessments.title: Contaminant fate coverage for dry treatment and composite extrusion
assessments.label: Minimal
assessments.rationale: The decision-relevant analytes and the major output streams have not been measured, and the located description contains no stage at which a contaminant could leave the material, so nothing is measured and nothing is removed.

assessments.title: Sink completeness for dry treatment and composite extrusion
assessments.label: Proposed
assessments.rationale: The material and the extrusion route are named, but no acceptance basis and no issuer have been located, and the route for the composite at end of life is undefined.

assessments.title: Product readiness for dry treatment and composite extrusion
assessments.label: Undefined
assessments.rationale: No mechanical testing data, no leaching behaviour and no product gate have been located for the composite, so there is no product performance evidence to judge.

assessments.title: Regulatory clarity for dry treatment and composite extrusion
assessments.label: Unlocated
assessments.rationale: No located source names a jurisdiction, a material status or an authority for this composite. Building codes, product rules and chemical rules would all have to be checked for any jurisdiction before this material could be used.

assessments.title: Validation maturity for dry treatment and composite extrusion
assessments.label: Foundational unknowns
assessments.rationale: Whether the containment holds over the product's life is a basic physical question that has to be answered before a bounded test against any product criterion can be defined.

gapNotes: No published blend ratio, extrusion temperature, screw speed or residence time exists for this family. Those parameters are inventor choices, not measured reference values.
No leaching, weathering or end-of-life study exists for a composite of this kind. Whether the sealed-in residues remain contained over the life of the product is unknown.
No energy consumption data exists for drying, milling or extrusion in this family, so per-unit figures cannot be estimated.

Evidence for this family is limited to company descriptions. No independent verification of product performance, safety or environmental benefit exists.

title: Solvent dissolution and polymer recovery
summary: The filter material is dissolved in a solvent so that it separates from paper, tobacco and ash, then precipitated again as a solid and dried. The route targets the valuable polymer itself rather than using the butt as filler.
mechanism: Dissolution of the cellulose acetate in a solvent, filtration of the insoluble residue, precipitation of the polymer by adding a non-solvent, washing to strip residual solvent and dissolved contaminants, drying, and in some processes recovery of the solvent by distillation.
feedstock: Spent cigarette butts, with the tobacco and paper either separated beforehand or left in. No located source states a mass basis for the butt feed.
preparation: Collection, and optionally the separation of tobacco and paper from the filter material before the solvent stage.
variants: solid-liquid extraction with organic solvent and polymer characterisation

steps.label: Solvent dissolution
steps.description: The filter material is dissolved in a solvent so that it separates from the paper, tobacco and ash. No located source states a solvent concentration, a temperature, a time or a solvent-to-feed ratio, and several of the named solvents carry regulatory obligations that a route description has to respect.

steps.label: Filtration
steps.description: The undissolved residue, consisting of paper, tobacco, ash and part of the contamination, is filtered out and becomes a contaminated solid stream.

steps.label: Precipitation
steps.description: The polymer solution is combined with a non-solvent, which is typically water, so that the cellulose acetate comes back out as a solid.

steps.label: Washing
steps.description: The precipitated solid is washed to remove residual solvent and dissolved contaminants. Whether the washing is thorough enough to remove the solvent traces has not been measured.

steps.label: Drying and solvent recovery
steps.description: The washed solid is dried to recover the polymer, and in some described processes the solvent and non-solvent mixture is distilled and reused. The energy demand of that recovery is described as a major unknown.

inputs.label: Spent cigarette butts
inputs.description: Butts as the source of the cellulose acetate to be recovered.

inputs.label: Organic solvent
inputs.description: A solvent in which cellulose acetate dissolves, such as acetone, N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone, dimethylacetamide or tetrahydrofuran. Several of these are regulated substances with handling, storage and disposal requirements.

inputs.label: Non-solvent for precipitation
inputs.description: Typically water, used to precipitate the polymer back out of the solution.

streams.label: Wash water from the precipitated solid

products.label: Recovered cellulose acetate
products.description: Powder, flake or pellet recovered by precipitation and drying, offered for textile, film and membrane applications. Its purity, molecular weight and residual toxicity have not been characterised.
products.intendedUse: Textiles, films and membranes are named as target applications, but no product standard accepts recovered cellulose acetate from this source and no source demonstrates performance in any of them.

sinks.material: Cellulose acetate recovered by solvent dissolution and re-precipitation, with purity and molecular weight not established.
sinks.intendedUse: Textile, film and membrane applications, as proposed in the located sources.
sinks.acceptanceBasis: Not established. No product standard, leaching limit or purity specification has been located for recovered cellulose acetate from this source.
sinks.issuer: Not established. No company, standard body or authority has been located as the issuer of an accepted product.
sinks.finalRoute: Not established. The filtration residue and the spent solvent mixture have no demonstrated final route, and the spent solvent carries the extracted toxins.

organizations.name: Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche
organizations.role: Research body whose patent offering describes acetone extraction, filtration, water precipitation and acetone recovery from cigarette butts and filters, and reports reuse of the recovered polymer in fabricated articles.

organizations.name: Cerdia
organizations.role: Company named as pursuing recovery of cellulose acetate from post-consumer mouthpieces, with a published patent family.

auditReferences.label: CNR cellulose acetate recovery patent offering

claims.title: A patent offering describes dissolving the filter polymer and precipitating it again with water
claims.proposition: A patent offering describes extracting cellulose acetate and nicotine from cigarette butts and filters with acetone, filtering the solution, precipitating the polymer by adding water, and recovering the acetone by boiling.

claims.title: A published study extracted cellulose acetate with organic solvents and characterised it
claims.proposition: A peer-reviewed study describes extracting cellulose acetate from cigarette butts with acetone or ethyl acetate, characterising the recovered polymer by infrared and thermogravimetric analysis, studying its degradation, and forming a transparent film from it.

claims.title: No located source reports how contaminants partition across this family's streams
claims.proposition: No located source reports what share of nicotine, tar components, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons or heavy metals ends up in the recovered polymer rather than in the filtration residue or the spent solvent.

claims.title: Heavy-metal removal in this family is unknown
claims.proposition: No located source reports whether heavy metals follow the dissolved cellulose acetate into the recovered polymer or stay in the insoluble residue, and no located source describes a step that would remove them.

claims.title: No jurisdiction-specific regulatory status has been located for this family
claims.proposition: No located source names a jurisdiction, a material status, an acceptance pathway or an authority for this family, so the regulatory position of the recovered material remains unlocated.

claims.title: Recovering a polymer is not the same as producing a usable product
claims.proposition: Because the located sources show that the polymer can be recovered and characterised but report neither contaminant partitioning nor any performance measurement, recovering the polymer says nothing about whether the recovered material could be used in any application.
claims.reasoning: The two located sources together establish recovery and characterisation. Neither addresses contaminant partitioning or product performance, so the gap between a recovered polymer and a usable product is not bridged by anything located. The inference is that the two questions are separate and both remain open.

gaps.title: Where do the extracted toxins go once the solvent is spent
gaps.question: When the filter polymer is dissolved and the solvent is later spent, what is in that solvent, and what route exists for it?
gaps.whyItMatters: The route moves contamination out of the polymer and into a liquid. If that liquid has no route, the process has moved the problem rather than solved it, and the contamination is now in a more concentrated and less visible form.
gaps.falsifierOrDecisionCondition: A located source that names the treatment route for the spent solvent, together with measured contaminant levels in it, would close this question.

gaps.title: An alkaline pulping route has no reviewed method page in this layer
gaps.question: An alkaline pulping route that takes the material towards cellulose rather than back to acetate is recorded in the project's method record, but it has not been given a reviewed method-family page in this layer. How does it compare with solvent dissolution?
gaps.whyItMatters: This page would otherwise read as a complete account of the chemical routes, when a second chemical route exists in the project's records and has not been assessed here.
gaps.falsifierOrDecisionCondition: A reviewed method page with its own claims, gaps and assessments would close this gap and show where the pulping route sits against solvent dissolution.

gaps.title: Some solvents in this family carry regulatory handling obligations
gaps.question: What does the choice of solvent add to the obligations of any later trial?
gaps.whyItMatters: A route description that names solvents without naming their handling obligations would make a route look simpler than it is to operate lawfully.
assumptions: The route would use one of the solvents named in the located sources.
No alternative solvent with a lighter regulatory profile has been located for this recovery.
gaps.falsifierOrDecisionCondition: If a located source documented an equivalent route using a solvent without those obligations, this note would no longer bind the design of any later trial.

assessments.title: Evidence strength for solvent dissolution and polymer recovery
assessments.label: Limited
assessments.rationale: The located support is a patent offering and a peer-reviewed study, with no independent verification of any performance claim and no published contaminant or cost data. The peer-reviewed characterisation gives the family more than the minimal band, but not the mixed band, because no independent party has reproduced it.

assessments.title: Process ease for solvent dissolution and polymer recovery
assessments.label: Difficult
assessments.rationale: The route needs dissolution, filtration, precipitation, washing, drying and in some designs solvent recovery by distillation, together with handling of regulated solvents and a solvent recovery step that has to run for the economics to hold. That is well beyond the moderate band.

assessments.title: Resource burden for solvent dissolution and polymer recovery
assessments.unknownReason: No located source reports solvent consumption, recovery rate, energy or water on a stated functional unit, and no comparable denominator exists across the families, so this criterion stays unknown.

assessments.title: Contaminant fate coverage for solvent dissolution and polymer recovery
assessments.label: Minimal
assessments.rationale: No located source measures where the named analytes go. The streams are described but their contents are not, so neither the decision-relevant analytes nor the major output streams have been measured.

assessments.title: Sink completeness for solvent dissolution and polymer recovery
assessments.label: Proposed
assessments.rationale: The dissolution, precipitation and drying route is named, but no acceptance basis and no issuer have been located for the recovered polymer, and the route for the spent solvent and the filtration residue is undefined.

assessments.title: Product readiness for solvent dissolution and polymer recovery
assessments.label: Undefined
assessments.rationale: Although the recovered polymer has been characterised in one study, its purity, residual solvent, molecular weight and residual toxicity are not established on a comparable basis and no product gate has been located, so there is no product performance evidence to judge.

assessments.title: Regulatory clarity for solvent dissolution and polymer recovery
assessments.label: Unlocated
assessments.rationale: No jurisdiction, material status or authority has been located for this route. The chemical regulation that applies to the solvents is a separate obligation from any end-of-waste status, and neither has been located.

assessments.title: Validation maturity for solvent dissolution and polymer recovery
assessments.label: Foundational unknowns
assessments.rationale: The partition of every named contaminant across the three streams is unresolved, and the recovery rate of the solvent is unknown, so the route's viability itself rests on basic measurements that have to come first.

gapNotes: No published protocol specifies solvent type, concentration, temperature, dissolution time, solvent-to-butt ratio or precipitation conditions for this family. Those parameters are inventor choices, not measured reference values.

The recovered cellulose acetate has not been characterised for purity, molecular weight or residual toxicity, and no product standard accepts it.

No regulatory pathway has been identified for this material. The reproductive toxicity of one of the named solvents under the chemical regulation of the European Union is a particular handling concern.
No cost data exists for this family. Solvent cost and recovery rate, polymer yield and wastewater treatment would dominate the operating economics, and all are unmeasured.
Evidence for this family is limited to patents and general polymer literature. No independent verification of any performance claim exists.
This family cannot close a four-field sink with the evidence located so far. All four fields have major gaps.
